title: How many independent units?
hook: A hundred pupils share ten classrooms. How much information is independent?

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: randomize whole schools instead of students and the effective sample shrinks.

misconception: Treating cluster trials as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: randomize whole schools instead of students and the effective sample shrinks.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: A trial has 100 pupils in 10 schools of size 10. With intraclass correlation .2, use design effect 1+(m−1)ρ. What approximate effective sample size follows?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-cluster-trials/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Design effect1+(m-1)rho. 100 pupils in10 groups,m10,rho.2 givesdesign effect2.8 and effective n35.714; rho0 gives100; rho1 gives10. Label approximation.

src/demos/probability/p100-cluster-trials/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Design effect1+(m-1)rho. 100 pupils in10 groups,m10,rho.2 givesdesign effect2.8 and effective n35.714; rho0 gives100; rho1 gives10. Label approximation.

claims.text: The correlated-school case retains effective n=35.714; independent pupils retain 100. The design effect is 2.8 because classmates supply partly overlapping information.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-cluster-trials/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Design effect1+(m-1)rho. 100 pupils in10 groups,m10,rho.2 givesdesign effect2.8 and effective n35.714; rho0 gives100; rho1 gives10. Label approximation.

claims.text: This equal-size approximation summarizes a mean-estimation variance penalty. Actual cluster-trial analysis also depends on cluster counts, unequal sizes and design details; 100 pupils do not automatically provide 100 independent observations.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-cluster-trials/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Design effect1+(m-1)rho. 100 pupils in10 groups,m10,rho.2 givesdesign effect2.8 and effective n35.714; rho0 gives100; rho1 gives10. Label approximation.

claims.text: If group size is 5 and ρ=1, what is the design effect? The formula gives 1+(5−1)×1=5; completely correlated group members act as one information unit.
